A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DynRefer. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison despite extensive rewriting and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original DynRefer benchmark results and ablations for captioning, attribute detection and region recognition.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds referring-reasoning, inference-speed and additional ablation results.

M1.justification: The nested-view construction, alignment module, Q-former, three decoders, losses and pHASH selection objective remain unchanged. The renamed inference procedure and additional instruction-tuned evaluation do not document a new algorithm or architectural component.

E1.justification: V2 adds referring reasoning on Ferret-Bench, with instruction tuning using LLaVA and Osprey datasets. This extends the task requirements to answering questions about referred objects while retaining the original captioning, recognition and attribute benchmarks.

E2.justification: V2 adds Groma and ControlCap to captioning comparisons, and ControlCap, PixelLLM and DetCLIPv3 to dense captioning. The new reasoning comparison includes Shikra, Kosmos-2, Ferret and Osprey. BLIP disappears from the OVAD comparison when matching v1 Appendix Table 12 to v2 Table 2; most other expanded rows already appeared in v1's appendix.

E3.justification: V2 introduces instruction-tuned reasoning evaluation, an inference-speed protocol on one A100 GPU, and additional backbone/LLM configurations in Table 6. It also tests four views and additional initialization and inference-prior controls. Existing benchmark metrics and the standard five-epoch, batch-512 training settings are retained.

E4.justification: New analyses test four-view scaling and pretrained-Q-former dependence, alignment under image-prior inference, and three-view task-prior selection (Tables 7–9). V2 also adds efficiency comparisons and selected-view/reasoning examples. The original fixed-region-view and nested-view ablations are moved into the main ablation table.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. Stochastic view sampling is part of the method, not an uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Headline DynRefer benchmark scores are retained, but v2 adds reasoning results, including 68.9 on Ferret-Bench, plus speed and additional ablation results. GLaMM's reported CIDEr changes from 105.0 to 106.0 on RefCOCOg and from 157.8 to 180.5 on VG. Figure 4 also changes the OVAD random-view reference from 27.5 to approximately 26.1.

T1.justification: The crop-interpolation construction and Equation 1 remain mathematically equivalent. Neither version supplies formal theoretical results or proofs; the removed manifold exposition and added optimization-complexity explanation are conceptual.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: resolution-adaptive referring, stochastic vision-language alignment, selective inference and strong multitask performance using one model. The added experiments support these claims without materially redefining them.

C2.justification: V2 removes the dedicated manifold discussion, attributes the four-view performance decline to optimization complexity, and explains the flexibility of image-prior selection. Dense-captioning performance is now described as comparable to DetCLIPv3. The stated limitation concerning imperfect imitation of human vision is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 explicitly identifies the default EVA backbone, three-view/image-prior inference, A800 memory capacity and A100 timing hardware. Most training hyperparameters and the code-access link remain unchanged. Figure 8 loses v1's explicit two-layer decoder specification.

R1.justification: V2 updates citations with works including FlexCap, Ferret, Groma, PixelLLM and DetCLIPv3, while removing the extended historical related-work appendix and some associated references. The central positioning around resolution adaptability and unified region-level tasks remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and inference explanation are extensively rewritten. Terminology changes from 'multi-modality' to 'multimodal,' training and inference headings become more explicit, the manifold section is removed, and decoder documentation and supplementary material are substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redraws architecture diagrams, transposes Figure 4's axes, and adds a radar chart, reasoning examples and view-selection visualizations. Benchmark and ablation tables are consolidated across main text and appendices. Appendix Tables 8–9 introduce reversed METEOR/CIDEr headers.

improvement.justification: New reasoning and speed evaluations, stronger comparison methods and targeted ablations improve the empirical assessment, while revised diagrams clarify view selection. These gains are tempered by limited documentation of the reasoning protocol and new METEOR/CIDEr labeling errors in appendix Tables 8–9 and the alignment discussion. With the core method and headline DynRefer results retained, the net improvement is useful but limited.
